why: v1.24.0 corrected a disk-bandwidth probe that was 6.8x too fast (warm page cache: cold 0.44 vs warm 2.99 GB/s). The OLD number was proven wrong; the NEW one has never been shown right, because all 14 ladder rows are VRAM- or RAM-resident and none reads the disk tier. This row closes that coverage gap.

machine_state.note_on_ram: The task brief said 32 GB RAM. wmic reports 17,122,660,352 B = 16 GiB. The tool auto-detects 16. 39.7 GB still vastly exceeds it either way, so the disk tier is genuinely exercised; recording the discrepancy rather than silently accepting the brief.
machine_state.C14: one cal_id for prediction AND measurement; if cal_id drifts before the bench, the stake is void

model.read_from_gguf: 117.5619776B total, 8.140974848B active, 3.705498368B always-active, 2.7 effective bits, 48 layers, KV 192 KB/pos, 92.6% I-quant tensors

printed_winner.why_not: The row's own warn says it needs an expert-caching runtime (ktransformers/colibri-class); stock llama.cpp b10098 cannot LRU experts in VRAM. Its 'flags' string is not a runnable llama.cpp command. This row is DECLARED UNMEASURABLE on this box and is NOT scored. No substitute estimate is offered.

row_under_test.why_this_row: The winner row's own warn names this as the row stock llama.cpp actually gets. It is the only disk-tier row the installed runtime can execute, and 93% of its predicted token is the disk-bandwidth term the v1.24.0 correction changed. It is therefore the row that tests the corrected number.

predictions_from_quantprobe_plan.binding_constraint_printed: IO-BOUND (disk I/O) - 96% of every decode token
predictions_from_quantprobe_plan.steady_state_assumption: The row's miss term is miss = 1 - (0.9 x RAM_eff)/size = 1 - 14.4/39.685 = 0.6371. The model therefore predicts a PARTIALLY WARM steady state in which ~36% of the model is page-cached in RAM and ~64% is re-read from disk every token. It does NOT predict a first-touch cold pass. Scoring must use steady-state repetitions, not the warmup.

emitted_command_trap_recorded_before_ben.problem: `plan` prints ONE 'run it:' line, for the winner row. Here that is '-ngl 99 + runtime-managed expert cache'. The ladder's flags_from_emit() would parse '-ngl 99' out of it and try to put a 39.7 GB model on a 6 GB card.
emitted_command_trap_recorded_before_ben.decision: Bench the row_under_test's own flags (-ngl 0) plus the emitted -b 2048 -ub 2048 --threads 4, which the plan prints for this machine. Recording this here, before measuring, so the choice is not a post-hoc convenience.

bench_protocol.primary_metric: tg64, same metric and r=2 the 14-row ladder uses
bench_protocol.gates: kill orphan llama-server/llama-bench; GPU < 1500 MiB; 3 consecutive CPU samples <= 25%
bench_protocol.mmap: left ON (default). A 39.7 GB file with --no-mmap on a 16 GB box cannot be allocated; mmap IS the disk-streaming mechanism under test.

KILL_RULES.KR1_band: PASS iff measured tg64 lies inside the tool's own printed +/-25% estimate band around the staked 0.331505 tok/s. Convention err_pct = (predicted - measured)/measured*100, identical to the locked ladder. |err_pct| <= 25 => measured in [0.265204, 0.442007] tok/s. Outside that interval is a FAIL, published at equal prominence, and the changelog must then disclose the disk-tier path as unvalidated.
KILL_RULES.KR2_load_time_contamination: The number must be DECODE, not load. Falsifier: run the identical harness at -n 32 as well as -n 64. llama-bench excludes model load from tg timing, so tok_s(32) and tok_s(64) must agree within 25%. If tok_s(32) is materially BELOW tok_s(64), fixed per-run overhead is leaking into the timing and the primary number is REPORTED AS DOMINATED BY LOAD, not scored.
KILL_RULES.KR3_harness_can_vary: Before trusting the harness, construct the input that makes it fail. Run the SAME parse/harness on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf at -ngl 0 (fits in RAM, no disk tier). It MUST report > 3.0 tok/s (the calibration pure-CPU anchor is 7.09). If it returns anything near 0.3, the harness is emitting a constant and NO verdict may be issued from it.
KILL_RULES.KR4_cold_vs_warm: Report rep-to-rep spread. If rep 1 and rep 2 differ by more than 2x, say so: the row is not in a steady state and the single mean is not the quantity the model predicts.
KILL_RULES.no_renegotiation: These rules are final as of the staked_utc above. A miss is published, not re-banded.
